solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Feeling dejected, cat bites leg

indicators.note: something that bites takes a mouthful, holding another word between its jaws

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable because the cat has bitten their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG holds PIN, giving MO-PIN-G.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to be listless and gloomy, so moping is a synonym for feeling low.

clue.text: Football legend is French, and most disorganised

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the Argentine footballer
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A legendary footballer who is French and very disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: Messiest is the superlative of messy, untidy, so it means the most disorganised.

clue.text: Spooner's green energy for strong building

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so we swap them here

parts.note: teal is a blue-green colour and power is energy; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner's campaign for renewable power to build something sturdy.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAL POWER with its first sounds swapped becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peel tower is a small fortified tower of the Scottish Borders, a strong defensive building.

clue.text: Call bloke up on phone at last

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of phone

explanation.surface: Finally ringing a man on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like phoning, but it is the definition: to give a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to name them.

clue.text: Occasional long film about lawgiver, leader of Israelites

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the film wraps round what follows

parts.note: an epic is a long, grand film

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Sod's Law, the British Murphy's Law, makes Sod a giver of a law
first letter of Israelites

explanation.surface: An occasional screening of a lengthy film about Moses, the lawgiver who led the Israelites.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints Moses, but the lawgiver is Sod, of Sod's Law, Britain's name for Murphy's Law (whatever can go wrong will).
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic happens in separate, irregular bursts, so it is occasional rather than continuous.

clue.text: Old man swallowing a tablet for small lump

indicators.note: swallowing takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pa is father, an old man
taken as written
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: Dad swallows a tablet to treat a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: PA holds A PILL: P-APILL-A.
explanation.definitionFit: A papilla is a small rounded bump, such as those on the tongue.

clue.text: It hangs in cave and, strangely, it lactates

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something dangling in a cave that oddly produces milk.
explanation.walkthrough: The milky drip fits: these formations grow from mineral-rich water dripping down.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is a column of mineral deposit hanging from a cave roof.

clue.text: Fruit drop picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a signal is picked up by ear

parts.note: to droop is to drop or sag

explanation.surface: Fruit that has fallen and been gathered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' fits the fruit picture but means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A drupe is a stone fruit such as a plum or cherry.

clue.text: Make councillor take Ecstasy

parts.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
to take a meal is to eat it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Forcing a local councillor to take ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To create something is to make it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Flan containing hot whiskey and Scotch

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so other letters sit within

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
H is the abbreviation for hot
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dessert tart laced with hot whiskey and Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' wants to be whisky, next to whiskey; it is the verb to put a stop to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to put an end to it, which is to thwart it.

clue.text: Has time at sea aboard special vessel

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
aboard means on board, held inside the other piece

parts.note: sp is an abbreviation of special
the letters of has time rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spends time at sea aboard a special boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go inside SP: S-TEAMSHI-P.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a ship driven by steam engines, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Entertain warm Aussie on regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An Australian who is warm and entertains people regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to keep them entertained, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Scrap section of Riot Act

indicators.note: a section of the phrase is a stretch of its letters, read straight through

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Tearing up part of the Riot Act, the old law against unruly crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb to tear up, but it is the noun: a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, means the tiniest amount, so a scrap.

clue.text: Legislature exercising paternalism, regardless of society

indicators.note: exercising puts something through its paces, working it into new shapes
regardless of means paying no heed to, so that letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A government that acts paternalistically without regard for society.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S out of PATERNALISM and rearrange the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is the elected law-making body of a country, a legislature.

clue.text: Some dreadful film entrepreneur's gratification

indicators.note: some of the words means a run of their letters, not all of them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A businessman takes pleasure in a terrible film.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulfilment is the satisfaction of a desire, so it is a kind of gratification.

clue.text: Result of cutting deal?

parts.note: surface reading: the outcome of reducing or cutting a business deal
setter's reading: deal is pine or fir timber, and sawing it leaves fine wood powder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting deal' sounds like negotiating a bargain; deal is also softwood timber, and the result of sawing it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawing timber leaves fine particles of wood behind, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Perhaps Constable and I start cycling

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round, moving one by one from the front to the back

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police constable and I begin a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the front letter to the back three times: STARTI, TARTIS, then the answer. John Constable was an English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was a famous painter, so he is an example of an artist, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Scoundrel caught partner dividing loot

indicators.note: dividing means splitting something apart by going into its middle

parts.note: swag is stolen goods
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A villain is caught with his accomplice sharing out the stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a rascal or rogue, a mild word for a scoundrel.

clue.text: Grubby earl, awful in the sack

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
E is an abbreviation for earl
grim means dreadful

explanation.surface: A dirty aristocrat who is terrible in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the sack' means go to bed, so the sack is slang for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Begrimed means covered in grime, so grubby and dirty.

clue.text: Benefit for Paddy

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a paddy is British slang for a temper tantrum, as is a fit

explanation.surface: A charity benefit organised for someone called Paddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a man's name; it is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit is to gain or benefit, and a profit is a benefit gained.

clue.text: Writer enthralled by wild nature of bulls

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters run loose
enthralled by means held captive by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the letters of nature rearranged
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: An author captivated by the wild nature of bulls.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside the rearranged letters: TAUR-I-NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurine is an adjective meaning relating to bulls, from Latin taurus, a bull.

clue.text: Can retrospectively tax fertiliser

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a tin is a can
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: A government able to tax fertiliser backdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning is able; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen salts widely spread on fields as fertiliser.

clue.text: Deny springing wife from old London prison

indicators.note: springing a prisoner frees them, so that letter escapes from the word

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious London jail, closed in 1902
w is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone denies helping his wife escape from an old London jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from NEWGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny it or declare it untrue.

clue.text: Undermine one's mate

parts.note: one's read as one is, which for the speaker is I'm
to mate is to pair

explanation.surface: Someone sabotaging a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it, so to undermine it.

clue.text: Came across pronounced antipathy for science

parts.note: to meet is to come across

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we want what the word sounds like rather than its spelling

parts.note: an allergy is an aversion or antipathy

explanation.surface: Someone who encountered a strong dislike of science.
explanation.walkthrough: MET followed by a word sounding like ALLERGY makes the answer when said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgy is the branch of science dealing with metals and their properties.

clue.text: Vehicle initially provided for vagrant

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, pointing to the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of provided

explanation.surface: Transport laid on at first for a homeless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, a synonym of vagrant.

clue.text: Slight mumble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an insult or smear on someone's name
second meaning: to speak indistinctly, running words together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective meaning small; here it is the noun for an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both an insulting remark and the act of speaking with words running together.

clue.text: Catch them bare, both unclothed

indicators.note: unclothed strips the outer layers, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: inner letters of them
inner letters of bare

explanation.surface: Catching a couple naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it.

clue.text: American beauties periodically fade

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: American beauty queens lose their looks from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or die away, as a storm or noise fades.

clue.text: Au fait with mines exploding

indicators.note: exploding blows something apart so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone knowledgeable about mines going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the swim means being up to date and involved, the idiom matching au fait, well-informed.

clue.text: Performed transplant on Kitty and Edward?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a kitty is a pot of pooled money
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A surgeon carried out a transplant on two people called Kitty and Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies RE; the transplant is a gardener's, moving plants to new pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to move it to a new pot, a gardener's kind of transplant.

clue.text: Returned spade after a day, not wanting it

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: to spade the ground is to dig it

explanation.surface: A spade handed back after a day because it was not wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the reversed piece behind FRI. 'It' is old slang for sex appeal or desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid describes someone with no sexual desire, 'it' being slang for sex.
